description_full: United Microelectronics Corporation operates as a semiconductor wafer foundry in Taiwan, China, Hong Kong, Japan, Korea, the United States, Europe, and internationally. It manufactures and sells integrated circuits. The company offers circuit design; mask tooling; wafer fabrication; and assembly and testing services for communication devices, consumer electronics, computer, and other applications. It also provides venture capital and marketing support; consulting and planning; energy technical; solar engineering integrated design; research and development services; and insurance services. United Microelectronics Corporation was incorporated in 1980 and is headquartered in Hsinchu City, Taiwan.

financial_summary: United Microelectronics Corpora is a large-cap technology business with a $38.6B market cap on $7.2B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -2% over the past three years — essentially flat, and a business treading water is rarely a path to compounding. Operating margins are expanding by +2.5pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 28% against a 10% cost of capital — a 18-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 27%.

The business throws off $166M in free cash flow — roughly 2 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.93× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 29× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield of 2.6% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.
